claims.text: The tested FeNiCrMn high-entropy alloy contains no Co.
The FeNiCrMn alloy has a microstructure optimized for corrosion resistance.
Instrumented nanoindentation can reveal measurable microscale heterogeneities in hardness and elastic modulus in FeNiCrMn.
Local hardness and elastic-modulus variations in FeNiCrMn correlate with microstructural features.
FeNiCrMn will have nanoindentation hardness and modulus values roughly comparable to similar Co-containing HEAs.
Relevant local microstructural variations may include grain-size differences, phase boundaries, and precipitates.
Nanoindentation induces localized elastic and plastic deformation.
Variations in nanoindentation hardness and elastic modulus reflect underlying microstructural inhomogeneities.
Alloy composition can affect local deformation and hardening behavior.
Processing history can produce microstructural differences in high-entropy alloys.
Nanoindentation will yield a distribution of hardness and elastic-modulus values across FeNiCrMn specimens.
Regions with refined microstructures or particular phase assemblages will exhibit elevated hardness.
Published nanoindentation studies on CoCrFeMnNi have successfully correlated localized mechanical properties with microstructural features.
Ambient laboratory nanoindentation results may not translate directly to bulk mechanical performance or extreme-environment behavior.
The magnitude of microstructural heterogeneity and nanoindentation properties may vary significantly with processing conditions.
Comparisons between FeNiCrMn and Co-containing HEAs are sensitive to compositional and processing differences.
